chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim narrated from Muhammad, from Ahmad, from Muthanna, from Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

"When a man is prevented (from completing Hajj) and sends his sacrificial animal, but his head is affected (by shaving or cutting hair) before he slaughters his animal, then he must slaughter a sheep in place of the one he was prevented with, or fast, or give charity to six poor people; and the fasting is three days, and the charity is half a Sa' for each poor person."

The Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: And whoever covers his head, upon him is a blood sacrifice (dam). And that has already passed in what preceded, and what increases its clarification is what he narrated:

key_terms.آذَاهُ رَأْسُهُ: His head was affected (by shaving/cutting hair)
key_terms.دَم: Blood sacrifice (specifically a sheep or camel)
key_terms.صَاع: A traditional unit of volume for food
key_terms.هَدْي: Sacrificial animal sent by the pilgrim

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for a pilgrim who cuts their hair before slaughtering their sacrificial animal due to being prevented?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* details the specific expiations (kaffarah) for a pilgrim prevented from completing Hajj who prematurely cuts their hair, offering a tiered choice between slaughtering a sheep, fasting three days, or feeding six poor people. Shaykh al-Tusi clarifies that these rulings apply to the 'prevented' pilgrim, while noting that voluntarily covering the head also incurs a blood sacrifice, reflecting the juristic distinction between involuntary impediment and voluntary transgression of Ihram conditions.
